name: ramose
description: Ramose — an immutable, Datomic-inspired graph database for Cloudflare (Workers + Durable Objects + R2), built on Effect. One package: portable authoring (`ramose/db`), Alchemy resources (`ramose`), the peer Worker (`ramose/worker`) and the Better Auth plugin (`ramose/better-auth`).
author: Tyler van Hensbergen <tvanhens@gmail.com>
//dependencies: Ramose owns its whole runtime graph on purpose: `bun add ramose` has to be
enough for the portable and deploy paths.
`effect` is a required peer because operation declarations accept public
Effect Schema values. That makes the import legal under pnpm and Yarn PnP
and guarantees one version supplies both Ramose and application codecs.
`acorn` compiles creation defaults into a closure-free declarative plan at
catalog assembly. It is a direct runtime dependency because `ramose/db`
performs that validation in every supported JavaScript environment.
`alchemy` is a real dependency, not a peer: it carries the `alchemy` CLI
the quickstart runs. Its types sit in the public deploy signatures, and
the 2.x line is still beta (no semver signal). The range is pinned to the
tested beta and bumped per release — not `>=x <3`, which would admit
every future 2.x beta. The workspace root pins the same tested version
(exact) so `bun update alchemy` cannot split two copies.
`better-auth` and `zod` are optional peers that only `ramose/better-auth`
touches. Apps using that subpath need both peers installed. The zod peer
is naming hygiene, not a smaller install: `better-auth` already depends
on zod, so it stays in the tree of any app that uses `ramose/better-auth`.
//sideEffects: The `./src/**` globs are load-bearing in this workspace, not leftovers.
The root tsconfig `paths` point `ramose/worker` at `src/`, so the peer
Worker is bundled from source here even though only `dist` ships. Alchemy
re-exports `default` from a generated entry, so the Durable Object classes
reach the bundle only as re-exports — drop these globs and esbuild treats
the modules as side-effect-free and tree-shakes `TransactorDO` /
`QueryReplicaDO` away. Cloudflare then rejects the upload: "New version of
script does not export class 'QueryReplicaDO'". The `./dist/**` globs are
the same statement for a consumer bundling the published package.
